articulo: S4 · What a Good Local Guide Changes in Torres del Paine
caption:
The first quality we look for in a guide is empathy, not how much they know.

In Torres del Paine, a good guide listens, sets the pace and reads the wind. Three things to look for before you choose.

The full guide is on our journal. Link in bio.

#torresdelpaine #patagonia #localguides #tailormadetravel #chileanpatagonia

campos.title: What a good guide changes in Torres del Paine
campos.subtitle: Three things we look for in the person leading your day
campos.alt: Hikers in Torres del Paine with mountains in the background

campos.title: Empathy comes before information
campos.body: A good guide in Torres del Paine listens first. Some travelers want to walk in silence for hours, others want to go deeper into biodiversity or history. Knowing a lot is the starting point. Knowing when to speak is the skill.
campos.alt: Hikers walking near a lake in Torres del Paine

campos.title: Reading the mountain, not the forecast
campos.body: In Torres del Paine, wind and quickly changing weather matter most day to day. Checking a forecast online is not enough. A guide has to understand the territory, its conditions and risks, with training that matches the activity.
campos.alt: A hiker in a meadow in Torres del Paine

campos.title: Making the most of the day
campos.body: Safety is the floor, not the ceiling. Depending on conditions, a guide in Torres del Paine might change the order of the viewpoints, choose a sheltered place to stop, or wait for the weather to open before moving on.
campos.alt: A trail in Torres del Paine National Park in autumn

campos.title: Ask before you plan
campos.body: Is the guide's training suited to this activity? Is it private or shared? Who is the reference office on the ground? We are happy to help you think it through.
